stem: A motor lifts a $50\text{ kg}$ load through a height of $12\text{ m}$ at constant speed in $20\text{ s}$. What is the useful power output of the motor? ($g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$)
A ball of mass $0.20\text{ kg}$ is dropped from a height of $2.0\text{ m}$ onto a hard floor. It rebounds to a height of $1.5\text{ m}$. Ignore air resistance and take $g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the kinetic energy of the ball just before it hits the floor.
markscheme: Loss of gravitational potential energy = gain in kinetic energy

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the fraction of the ball's energy that is lost in the bounce.
markscheme: Energy after bounce $= mg \times 1.5$; energy lost $= mg \times 0.5$

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest what happens to the energy that is lost.
markscheme: Transferred to internal (thermal) energy of the ball and floor and/or to sound
